userMessage: Build an ESP32-based vibration monitor using an MPU6050. It should stream acceleration telemetry and analyze stationary sensor noise to verify that accel_x RMS noise stays below 0.10 g.

generate-project-brief.goal: Design and prototype an ESP32-based vibration monitor that continuously streams acceleration telemetry from an MPU6050 and verifies that stationary accel_x RMS noise remains below 0.10 g.
generate-project-brief.problemStatement: Vibration monitoring applications require both real-time telemetry streaming and confidence that the sensor's own noise floor does not corrupt measurements. Without a verified noise baseline, false vibration detections caused by sensor noise cannot be distinguished from genuine mechanical events. This project addresses that gap by combining live acceleration telemetry with a stationary noise-verification routine that enforces a 0.10 g RMS threshold on the accel_x axis.
generate-project-brief.intendedContext: An embedded prototype built around a user-specified ESP32 microcontroller and MPU6050 inertial sensor, intended for early-stage concept validation of a vibration monitoring device. The device will operate in a stationary position during noise-verification runs and in a vibration-exposed position during normal telemetry streaming.
scope: Integrate the ESP32 with the MPU6050 to acquire raw acceleration data on all three axes.
Implement continuous acceleration telemetry streaming from the ESP32 to an external destination.
Implement a stationary noise-analysis routine that computes accel_x RMS noise over a defined capture window.
Enforce a pass/fail verdict against the 0.10 g RMS noise threshold for accel_x.
Define and document the sampling rate and capture duration used for the noise-verification routine.
Validate end-to-end data flow from sensor acquisition through telemetry output.
outOfScope: Enclosure design or mechanical mounting engineering.
Detailed component selection beyond the user-specified ESP32 and MPU6050.
Analysis of axes other than accel_x for the RMS noise threshold (unless later extended by the user).
successCriteria: The device successfully acquires acceleration data from the MPU6050 on all three axes without data loss during normal streaming operation.
Acceleration telemetry is streamed continuously to an external destination at a defined and documented sampling rate.
The stationary noise-analysis routine computes accel_x RMS noise over a defined capture window and produces a repeatable result.
The accel_x RMS noise measured during stationary verification is confirmed to be below 0.10 g, yielding a clear pass verdict.
A result above 0.10 g produces a clear fail verdict, distinguishable from a pass result.
The noise-verification routine and telemetry streaming mode can each be invoked reliably in a prototype build.

assumptions.statement: The microcontroller is an ESP32, as explicitly stated by the user.
The inertial sensor is an MPU6050, as explicitly stated by the user.
The device must stream acceleration telemetry to an external destination.
The accel_x RMS noise threshold for the stationary verification routine is 0.10 g, as explicitly stated by the user.
The noise-verification routine is performed with the sensor held stationary (no intentional mechanical excitation).
Telemetry streaming and noise-verification are two distinct operational modes of the same device.
The project is at the concept stage and targets a prototype build, not a production release.
The noise-verification result will be expressed as a pass/fail verdict; the specific output mechanism (alert, log entry, display, etc.) has not yet been defined.
A single capture window of fixed duration and fixed sampling rate will be used for the RMS noise computation; these parameters are to be defined during prototype planning.

requirements.statement: The system shall use an ESP32 as the host microcontroller.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly stated the ESP32 as a fixed hardware constraint.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of hardware design and bill of materials.

requirements.statement: The system shall use an MPU6050 inertial measurement unit as the acceleration sensor.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly stated the MPU6050 as a fixed hardware constraint.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of hardware design and bill of materials.

requirements.statement: The system shall continuously stream acceleration telemetry data (at minimum the X, Y, and Z axes) to an external destination.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly required streaming of acceleration telemetry.
requirements.verificationMethod: Functional test: confirm telemetry packets containing acceleration data are received at the destination during device operation.

requirements.statement: The system shall operate a stationary noise analysis mode in which it captures a sequence of accel_x samples and computes the RMS noise value.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly required analysis of stationary sensor noise on the accel_x axis.
requirements.verificationMethod: Functional test: place device on a stable, vibration-free surface, trigger noise analysis mode, and confirm an RMS value is computed and reported.

requirements.statement: The accel_x RMS noise measured during stationary noise analysis shall remain below 0.10 g.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly stated the 0.10 g RMS threshold as a verification criterion for accel_x noise.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: with the device stationary on a vibration-isolated surface, run the noise analysis routine and verify the reported accel_x RMS value is strictly less than 0.10 g.
acceptanceCriteria: accel_x RMS noise value is less than 0.10 g during stationary capture.
The result is produced and accessible (logged, reported, or transmitted) at the end of each noise analysis run.

requirements.statement: The system shall produce a clear pass/fail indication for the accel_x RMS noise verification result, distinguishing whether the measured value is below or at/above the 0.10 g threshold.
requirements.rationale: Verifying a threshold necessarily implies the system must report whether the threshold was met or exceeded; the specific output mechanism (alert, log, display) was not stated.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: induce conditions that produce RMS noise both below and above 0.10 g and confirm the system correctly classifies each case.

requirements.statement: The system shall acquire accel_x samples for noise analysis at a defined, consistent sampling rate sufficient to characterize the sensor noise floor.
requirements.rationale: Computing a meaningful RMS noise figure requires a defined sampling rate and capture duration; neither was specified by the user.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of firmware configuration and test: verify sample timestamps confirm the configured rate is maintained throughout a noise capture window.

requirements.statement: The system shall transmit telemetry data over a defined communication interface to a receiving host or service.
requirements.rationale: Streaming telemetry to an external destination implies a communication interface; the transport protocol and destination were not specified.
requirements.verificationMethod: Integration test: confirm telemetry data is received and parseable at the designated host endpoint.

requirements.statement: The system shall maintain telemetry streaming with a latency low enough that acceleration data is useful for vibration monitoring purposes.
requirements.rationale: A vibration monitor is only useful if telemetry is delivered with sufficiently low latency; no specific latency figure was stated by the user.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: measure end-to-end latency from sensor sample acquisition to receipt at the destination and confirm it meets the agreed target.

requirements.statement: The system shall be powered by a supply source compatible with the operating environment and shall sustain continuous telemetry streaming and noise analysis without power interruption.
requirements.rationale: Any embedded device requires a defined power source; the user did not specify power supply type, voltage, or budget.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: operate the device under full load (streaming + noise analysis) for a defined duration and confirm no power-related resets or failures occur.

requirements.statement: The system shall remain operational across the expected ambient temperature range of the deployment environment.
requirements.rationale: No operating environment was described; a temperature range requirement is standard for embedded hardware but cannot be confirmed without user input.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: operate the device at the boundary temperatures of the specified range and verify correct function.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a means to distinguish between noise analysis mode and normal telemetry streaming mode, ensuring both modes can be invoked in a controlled and repeatable manner.
requirements.rationale: Having two distinct operational modes (streaming and noise analysis) implies a need for a reliable mechanism to select and trigger each mode; no UI or control interface was specified.
requirements.verificationMethod: Functional test: invoke each mode via the defined control mechanism and confirm the correct mode activates each time.

requirements.statement: The noise analysis result, including the computed accel_x RMS value and the pass/fail determination, shall be persisted or transmitted so it is accessible after the analysis run completes.
requirements.rationale: Verification of a threshold implies the result must be observable; whether this is via local log, serial output, or telemetry channel was not stated.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: run noise analysis and confirm the RMS value and pass/fail result are retrievable from the designated output (log, display, or telemetry stream).

requirements.statement: All requirements shall be verified through documented test procedures before the prototype is considered complete.
requirements.rationale: Nexus workflow policy requires that all requirements carry a verification method and that verification is completed at prototype closure.
requirements.verificationMethod: Review of completed test records against each requirement's defined verification method.

generate-requirements.requirementSummary: Fourteen requirements have been derived for the ESP32 + MPU6050 vibration monitor. Five are confirmed user-explicit requirements covering the ESP32 and MPU6050 as fixed hardware constraints, continuous acceleration telemetry streaming, stationary accel_x noise analysis, and the hard 0.10 g RMS noise ceiling. Two user-implied requirements address the necessary pass/fail reporting of the threshold result and the need for a defined sampling rate and capture window for the noise analysis. Five system-inferred requirements (marked proposed) cover the telemetry communication interface, streaming latency, power supply continuity, operating temperature range, and mode-selection usability. One project-policy requirement mandates documented verification of all requirements at prototype closure. Six dimensions remain unresolved and are listed in missingDimensions.

generate-functional-architecture.systemBoundary: The system boundary encompasses all functional subsystems resident on the ESP32-based vibration monitor device: inertial sensing, raw data acquisition, noise analysis, telemetry streaming, status indication, and power supply. The boundary excludes any remote host, dashboard, or cloud service that receives the telemetry stream.

nodes.name: Inertial Sensing Subsystem
responsibilities: Acquire raw three-axis acceleration samples from the MPU6050 (user-stated constraint) at a configurable sampling rate.
Acquire raw three-axis gyroscope samples from the MPU6050.
Maintain the sensor in a known, stable operating configuration (full-scale range, digital low-pass filter setting) suitable for noise characterization.
Deliver timestamped sample frames to the data acquisition subsystem on demand or via interrupt.

nodes.name: Data Acquisition and Buffering Subsystem
responsibilities: Receive timestamped acceleration and gyroscope frames from the inertial sensing subsystem.
Buffer a configurable window of samples in volatile memory for downstream processing.
Enforce a defined capture duration and sample count for stationary noise analysis windows.
Provide sample streams concurrently to both the noise analysis subsystem and the telemetry formatting subsystem.

nodes.name: Noise Analysis Subsystem
responsibilities: Receive a stationary sample window from the data acquisition subsystem.
Compute the RMS value of the accel_x channel over the captured window.
Compare the computed accel_x RMS against the 0.10 g threshold.
Produce a pass/fail verdict and the numeric RMS result.
Forward the verdict and result to the status reporting subsystem and the telemetry formatting subsystem.

nodes.name: Telemetry Formatting Subsystem
responsibilities: Receive live acceleration sample frames from the data acquisition subsystem.
Receive noise analysis results (RMS value, pass/fail verdict) from the noise analysis subsystem.
Serialize acceleration telemetry and noise analysis results into a structured, transmittable payload.
Pass formatted payloads to the communication subsystem for transmission.

nodes.name: Communication Subsystem
responsibilities: Accept serialized telemetry payloads from the telemetry formatting subsystem.
Manage the transport-layer connection to the external telemetry destination (transport method to be determined).
Stream telemetry payloads to the external destination continuously or at a defined reporting interval.
Report connection status back to the status reporting subsystem.

nodes.name: Status Reporting Subsystem
responsibilities: Receive noise analysis pass/fail verdicts from the noise analysis subsystem.
Receive communication link status from the communication subsystem.
Present device operational state and noise verification outcome to the user via a local indicator (indicator type to be determined).
Distinguish at minimum: normal operation, noise threshold exceeded, and communication fault states.

nodes.name: Power Supply Subsystem
responsibilities: Accept energy from an external or onboard power source (source type to be determined).
Regulate and distribute appropriate voltage and current rails to the processing, sensing, communication, and indication subsystems.
Maintain stable power delivery within the operating envelope of all subsystems.

nodes.name: System Control and Orchestration Subsystem
responsibilities: Coordinate startup sequencing of all subsystems.
Trigger stationary noise analysis windows at defined intervals or on demand.
Manage transitions between continuous telemetry streaming mode and noise analysis capture mode.
Handle fault conditions reported by any subsystem and initiate appropriate recovery or shutdown actions.

assumptions.statement: The ESP32 is accepted as the processing platform per the user's explicit statement; no other processing unit is assumed.
The MPU6050 is accepted as the inertial sensor per the user's explicit statement; no alternative sensor is assumed.
The 0.10 g RMS threshold applies specifically to the accel_x channel as stated; thresholds for accel_y and accel_z are not defined and are not enforced by this architecture.

The telemetry transport method (wired vs. wireless, protocol, destination) has not been specified; the communication subsystem is designed transport-agnostic and the specific transport remains an open decision.

The noise analysis is performed on a stationary device; the architecture assumes a dedicated stationary capture window distinct from live vibration monitoring, triggered by the orchestration subsystem.
The sampling rate and capture window duration for noise analysis are configurable parameters; specific values are not fixed at this stage.

A noise threshold violation (accel_x RMS ≥ 0.10 g) produces both a local status indication and an entry in the outgoing telemetry; whether it also triggers an alert or halts operation is not yet decided.
The power source type (USB, battery, regulated bench supply, etc.) is not specified; the power supply subsystem is designed source-agnostic.
All three acceleration axes are buffered and streamed as telemetry, even though only accel_x is subject to the RMS noise threshold requirement.

The type of local status indicator (visual, audible, display, or none) for the status reporting subsystem has not been decided.
